name: Aurora Gradients / Glassmorphism
visualIdentity: Frosted panels over slow aurora bands, diffuse fields, or mesh gradients. Use fine borders, highlights, soft shadows, and sharp foreground text; optional local refraction or dispersion. Keep brightness stable and avoid banding, shimmer, excessive blur, and competing backgrounds. This is distinct from Liquid Glass.
suitableUses: Explicitly suits ambient hero screens and calm brand moments. Suggested hybrids support app launches, feature reveals, settings walkthroughs, and premium dashboards. Inferred: useful for serene product explainers or interactive HTML interfaces where legible panels sit over atmospheric color.
limitations: Maintain two to four main aurora colors; don’t let blur or moving light compromise reading. For data, use sufficiently opaque panels, stable brightness, and primary accents only; avoid gradient-filled chart marks and data directly over aurora. Suitability for print-fixed layouts is unspecified.
palette: Suggested fallback: #142535 background, #F2F6F4 foreground, and three main aurora accents: #7FAAD0 blue, #9B87C3 violet, #65AAA5 teal. This fits the two-to-four main-color limit; background and foreground are supporting roles. Exact task, brand, reference, and existing semantic colors take precedence. Don’t recolor assets or expand approved colors. Optional Lab interpolation applies only to the aurora background; inspect actual compositing because opaque contrast ratios don’t validate glass or lighting.
motionAndInteraction: Keep the aurora slow and stable; move panels precisely. For video, derive every state from shared seekable time, seed procedural noise, and verify direct and reverse seeks. Interactive HTML may add scroll-driven card stacks or chapter handoffs, swipe-and-snap tracks, pointer tilt, or progress-led storytelling only when the content supports them; provide coherent reverse states and accessible alternatives. Orb deformation is an optional metaphor, not a default feature.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required audio layer. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence to fit the subject and explicit requirements. Tilt does not imply playback or spatial audio; voice cards need real audio and separate playback controls. For video, synchronize and mix through the chosen render pipeline and check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Use supplied exact colors and approved artwork unchanged. Keep text in a separate DOM layer. Recommended visual construction is a full-screen WebGL/GLSL aurora field with CSS backdrop-filter panels; use SVG or screen-space displacement only when refraction is needed. Seed noise, inspect rendered filters, and load fonts/assets before rendering. Other asset requirements are unspecified.
combinations: Compatible suggested pairings: style-095 interface motion for crisp panel states over slow aurora, with focus outlines and solid-fill fallback when backdrop-filter is unsupported; style-097 simple charts in opaque frosted cards, using one primary accent per series. Motion references are optional and must fit the scene. Avoid bouncy UI springs, low-contrast blur, hidden essential copy, unclear data ordering, or conflicting progress drivers.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion method for the style and action first: WebGL/GLSL for fields, HTML/CSS for panels and typography; GSAP is the primary seekable timeline, Motion is optional only with verified synchronization. HyperFrames owns composition, timing, media/audio sync, checks, and export. Remotion is allowed only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked; document why. Keep one owner per animated property and integrate deterministic layers or baked assets. For interactive HTML, bind live scroll or pointer behavior separately from video timing. Library combinations are optional, not a required bundle.
